ABOUT WORD TRAILS

A first view into word histories.

This midterm prototype supports tracing recorded etymological paths, comparing expressions for a concept, and inspecting the sources behind a connection.

What is included?

All 74,635 lexical records and 46,351 etymological links from your DiACL lexical export. Family grouping uses the supplied language tree: 450 of 466 lexical language records are mapped. The remaining records stay available as “Unmapped in tree.”

How to read it

  • Arrows are recorded word relationships, not language-family edges.
  • An asterisk marks a reconstructed form; placeholder nodes are labeled separately.
  • Graph depth counts recorded links, not years. Some links skip intermediate stages.
  • The map shows representative language locations, not exact transmission routes.
  • Matching a concept does not automatically establish cognacy.
  • Missing records do not prove a word or relationship did not exist.

Data & sources

Lexical export: 24 October 2026. Language tree: 23 October 2026. Word-list structure: 28 October 2026. Word-entry and relationship references remain separately inspectable.

The separate 422-row CSV is a metadata subset. The grammar export covers 17 Austronesian languages; it is reserved for future work and is not used to infer etymology.
